text:
anya: Heads up — seeing east-west p95 jumps during the batch flush window in us-west-2 around 03:10 UTC. Trader batchers hit ~37ms p95 (normal ~2-3ms). Anyone else noticing?

mike: yep, on grafana the spike lines up with the batcher flush panel -> https://grafana.redwood.example/d/cluster/ew-latency?orgId=1&from=now-1h

sanjay: checked node-gpu-14/15, rx_dropped spikes correlate. ethtool shows RX overrun counters spiking during that window.

nora: are we sure it's TCP not RDMA? dedicated pools use RDMA but these pods fall back to TCP when kernel-level path congests.

sanjay: we're on mlx5 driver on those hosts. RDMA enabled on some NICs but the traffic pattern is lots of short fanouts from batcher -> KV cache reads -> small reply bursts.

anya: timeline: batcher flush every 10s, we saw a massive concurrent fanout at 03:10:00 that coincides with p95 jump.

mike: ran quick iperf between node-gpu-14 -> node-gpu-15 during a repro window, results show jitter/loss.

mike: ```
iperf3 -c 10.2.3.15 -t 10
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth       Retr
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  1.05 GBytes   902 Mbits/sec  43

# retransmits non-zero during the spike window
```

infra-bot: Alert: PacketLoss:cluster-usw2-gpu raised for node-gpu-14 at 2026-03-17T03:10:05Z (alert-id: pktloss-1890123456)

sanjay: ethtool -S ens1f0 shows:

sanjay: ```
rx_no_buffer: 172
rx_missed: 84
rx_over_errors: 172
tx_aborted_errors: 0
```

nora: could be NIC rx-ring exhaustion + GRO/GSO oddities when bursts of small packets hit the stack. We saw similar behavior in a previous app when GRO aggregated too aggressively and queues popped.

anya: any quick mitigations we can try during peak window?

nora: suggestions:
- increase RX ring (ethtool -G)
- tune net.core.rmem_default/rmem_max and net.core.netdev_max_backlog
- disable GRO as a canary on 1 node to see effect

mike: tried disabling GRO on a test node (node-gpu-99) and re-ran the batcher; p95 on that node dropped from 36ms -> 4ms during the next flush.

mike: command used:
```
ethtool -K ens1f0 gro off
```

sanjay: trying rx-ring increase now on two repro nodes, bumping rx 4096 -> 16384 as a test.

sanjay: ```
ethtool -G ens1f0 rx 16384 tx 4096
# applied
```

anya: nice. Any clue if this is switch-side buffering / ECN / CoDel causing retransmits? Network team logs?

nora: asked network team for switch counters for the leafs handling these racks — they requested exact 10s window timestamps. I shared 03:09:55-03:10:15.

infra-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window for kernel/driver upgrades tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC (canary hosts only).

sanjay: driver candidate (mlx5 5.12.4) purportedly fixes rx-ring handling under bursty small packet workloads. We'd need canary rollout.

mike: short-term: rollout GRO off + rx ring bump to affected pool only during peak windows, confirm improvements, then decide on driver roll.

nora: also proposing eBPF flow sampling to capture per-flow packet rates during flush to confirm it's a fanout storm and not a pathological single flow.

anya: action items:
- sanjay: run GRO-off + rx-ring bump experiment on 5 repro nodes across two racks (today, followup in 2h)
- nora: open ticket with network team for switch buffer dumps + request whether PFC or Priority Flow Control is enabled on those leafs
- mike: coordinate canary kernel/driver rollout with infra-bot scheduled window

mike: quick note — this is only observed in us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool during heavy batching. non-dedicated pools not impacted so far.

anya: thanks all. please post any findings here; if GRO-off looks good we'll script an automated temporary toggle for the next few batch windows.

nora: adding: if GRO-off helps, long-term we still want a kernel/driver fix because GRO impacts CPU and throughput characteristics differently. GRO is a band-aid.

sanjay: experiment started, will post raw counters and a short log snippet after the next flush.

mike: thx — ping me if you want me to flip any nodes or look at grafana panels.

anya: closing loop: we'll reconvene after the experiment results. :thumbsup:
